prompt:
Create a production ANIMATION KEYFRAME REFERENCE SHEET for a realistic medieval first person game. Match the attached mercenary's worn charcoal padded sleeves, brown leather forearm bracers, fingerless leather gloves, natural individual fingers, steel sword in RIGHT hand, wooden round shield STRAPPED to LEFT forearm and gripped with LEFT hand. Actual human with head, torso, both shoulders, articulated upper arms, elbows, wrists and hands connected anatomically; these are NOT isolated weapon views.
ONE ACTION ONLY: RIGHT DIAGONAL CUT: right-handed swordsman winds up beside his RIGHT temple, blade pointing upward/back, then delivers one descending diagonal cut from his upper RIGHT to lower LEFT, follows through with his RIGHT fist across his torso on the LEFT at waist height, then recovers upright right ready. The LEFT shield retracts to protect the left ribs and tilts clear of the sword path.
Layout exactly 4 ROWS x 4 COLUMNS. Each column is an actual DISTINCT temporal key pose: PREPARE, CUT, FOLLOW, RECOVER. Each row films these SAME four temporal poses from a different fixed camera:
ROW 1 TOP: EXTERNAL bird's-eye camera above his head, looking straight down; scalp/shoulder tops visible, sword sweep visible in floor plane.
ROW 2 BOTTOM: EXTERNAL camera below waist looking up at chin/undersides of arms; no first-person view.
ROW 3 LEFT: EXTERNAL true left side PROFILE facing SCREEN RIGHT, left shield nearest camera.
ROW 4 RIGHT: EXTERNAL true right side PROFILE facing SCREEN LEFT, right sword arm nearest camera. Must be visibly opposite profile to row3; DO NOT duplicate left profile or swap hands.
Include chest and head in ALL panels to anchor view directions. Human faces fixed world forward, cameras orbit him; not turning his body to face all cameras. A small R sewn on right upper sleeve and L on left identifies handedness consistently. Full sword and shield in frame. No motion blur, no speed trails, no ghost limbs. Natural biomechanics, shoulder rotation drives elbow then wrist, firm but not stiff grip, anatomically plausible elbow bending, shield never passes through sword or body. Neutral dark grey studio, clear soft white grazing lighting. High detail photoreal game character. Small accurate labels on margins. Temporal distinctions and correct opposite cameras are more important than labels.
